proposed_facts.reason: Canonical teardown forwards grab_victim and the float to conditionally executed player-bookkeeping helpers, conditionally writes numeric destroy_type 0, clears both victim fields, and unconditionally calls cleanup and destruction. This corrects unsupported unregistration semantics.

Construction is fallible and returns zero on failure; the hitbox helper accumulates enabled-hitbox maximum damage from zero. Both item-spit callers pass the constructor result directly into old-item teardown and subsequently clear retained-item pointers, without a success guard. The old item's fighter association must not be conflated with the replacement projectile.

Kirby's target_item_gobj branches construct the replacement and destroy the retained item; item-drink also invokes teardown. The victim_gobj branches instead invoke the separate fighter-handling inline routine.

The implementation has one state-table row, guarded construction, lifetime decrement before expiry testing, XY speed-dependent scaling with an X-only fallback, collision-result forwarding, and delegated reference cleanup. Canonical Kirby callers establish item-spit and item-drink integration. The functionality document preserves these distinctions and exceptional behavior.
